title: Information Bounds for Two-Stage Treatment Regime Values with Scarce Jointly Labeled Data
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4; not salvageable within scope.

The minimax theorem matches only the joint-label rate orders, not the law-specific constant A(p)

proof_attempt_summary: D0 closed the exact four-mask information, interaction-kernel, ratio-uniform inference, minimax-rate, and adaptive-allocation claims; both D0.5 panel reviews passed. F1-F3 produced a Lean scaffold and attempted proof filling, but formalization had not reached F4/F5 when the cold general referee capped novelty below the field floor. A future field-tier program needs broader policy/model transfer or another substantive advance.
tldr: For a fixed response-dependent two-stage policy in the saturated positive binary model, the note derives the exact finite-count four-mask Fisher bound and identifies the exact sixteen-dimensional interaction kernel invisible to every nonjoint mask. That kernel yields the sharp residual constant \(A(p)/n_B\), a matching all-procedure joint-label minimax floor, and a complete policy-label elbow: constant second-stage rules separate across the single-label margins, whereas both response-dependent binary rules require joint labels. One observable pilot-weighted affine generalized least-squares estimator and Wald interval attain the exact bound uniformly while only \(n_B\) must diverge and all auxiliary count ratios vary arbitrarily. The same pilot architecture adaptively attains the finite-horizon cost oracle for arbitrary \(N_T/T\), including nonunique and boundary optima and the kernel-restricted \(F_\infty^*\) limit when unlabeled trajectories dominate. Standard longitudinal assumptions identify the causal value; the contribution is sharp estimation, inference, and annotation design.
gap: Classical known-marginal efficiency treats a bivariate law with effectively infinite auxiliary marginal information, while modern incomplete-data efficiency theorems impose finite positive pattern ratios or a positive complete-pattern share. Existing semi-supervised DTR theory uses complete reward labels, and the repository's one-stage discrete-ATE annotation frontier has no response-dependent second-stage action or distinct \(R\)-only and \(Y\)-only masks.
fill: The project starts with the exact finite-count four-mask information bound, proves the unrestricted-ratio interaction floor and a uniformly attaining estimator and interval, establishes the matching all-procedure joint-label minimax rate, and derives the cost allocation certificate from that statistical kernel.
